releases.notes: The community feed now enforces on every deployment. It shipped enforced by the three nginx map files the module includes, so a forward-auth install - Apache, or stock nginx behind the check - read them never: it pulled the shared list on schedule, listed every entry in the admin and marked them enforced, while every listed client walked straight through. The daemon now builds its matcher by reading back those same map files, so both wires answer from the same bytes and a hit is enforced in-process the moment the pull lands. A hit was also reported as nothing at all: it was folded into the protected-path variable, so it reached the visitor disguised as a protected path and arrived with force_reason=none on whatever chain the install defaults to - it is now its own axis, reported as community_bans with the match kind that caught the client. On an install whose default chain is pow_only a hit could re-challenge forever, because it raised the CAPTCHA-grade requirement without choosing the screen; the action now drives both. And that action is yours to pick - pow_only, captcha_only, pow_then_captcha or deny, defaulting to captcha_only, applied identically on the module and forward-auth. The rescues that must outrank it (verified search bots, bypass IPs and paths, a valid pass cookie) are still consulted first. Also fixed: a black-listed user-agent met a different challenge depending on deployment mode, because the forward-auth axis kept a fixed captcha_only from before the ua-filter picker existed while every other path and every screen inherited the install default; retention pruning issued one unbounded DELETE that rolled back on large tables, so nothing was ever deleted while the transaction left the ban lookup failing open; hunt showed the backend port behind a TLS-terminating load balancer instead of the visitor's; and a tab's inherited labels went stale while you were editing, naming the old default until a save reloaded the page.

A protected path that asks for a CAPTCHA now gets one. The 'unmask itself' preset ships on by default and puts a challenge in front of /unmask/admin/, but the pass-cookie exemption asked for a CAPTCHA-grade cookie only when the user-agent sat on a captcha-ending rule - it never consulted the protected path. A client holding a proof-of-work cookie, which a headless solver mints for itself, therefore walked through a captcha-graded protected path under an ordinary browser user-agent; both deployment modes now enforce the grade on the protected axis too. A protected path's mode is also the challenge it runs now: pow, captcha, or the new default pow_then_captcha, replacing a mode that only chose the match while the served chain came from a separate default action, a per-preset override, and failing those the rate-limit tab - so the admin gate could change because an unrelated tab was edited. The strict mode, documented as 'behaves like captcha for now' since 0.1, is gone with those inheritance layers. The rest is retention: raw events are the only thing the retention window still governs (the bot-hunt log, --ref lookups, rankings, analyze), so its default drops from 30 days to 7 - measured on a high-volume install that is ~8 GB against ~33 GB, and a full disk is a hard failure a default must not cause. Existing installs keep their stored value. The two things that still followed the raw window no longer do: the per-crawler trend sparkline moved to the same fixed 32-day aggregate as every other chart, and sites you declare in Site settings get their own funnel aggregates, so a declared site's 30-day funnel is independent of retention. The retention tab now projects the database's growth against the free space on its volume and warns when the disk is on course to fill. Also: hunt records the Referer of a challenged request, so you can see whether someone navigating in from your own pages hit a challenge.

This release adds an upgrade safety net for a growing operator base. On the review policy - the default for fresh installs - a new default-on enforcement preset that a later release adds (a challenge, deny or honeypot) stays inert until you acknowledge the upgrade, so a plain package upgrade never silently tightens what your site blocks: the dashboard shows a banner naming each held preset with one button to review and apply them, the same is available headless with unmask upgrade-review, and unmask doctor flags a pending review. Rescue presets (search-bot IP ranges, bypass paths) are never held. This replaces the old per-install seen_version gate, which held every new preset inert until the settings page was re-saved and drifted between nodes - a shipped preset is now active from the release that ships it on every install, with seen_version kept only for the settings UI's 'new since your last save' badge; existing installs default to apply, so their behavior is unchanged. Also: an opt-in GCP load-balancer health-check stats-exclude preset drops Google Cloud's health probes from the dashboard and bypasses the challenge in one toggle, and every preset in the settings UI now carries a 'since vX.Y.Z' version label. Fixed: a request context cancelled by a client disconnect no longer logs an event or audit insert as an error.

This release is mostly the settings surface. Text you type into a rule now survives a rejected save: across every settings tab, a save turned back for a self-lockout or an invalid pattern keeps your input, opens only the rows you changed, and marks the offending row with the reason - previously the page returned the last-saved list and the entry you were fixing was gone. The admin-host allowlist now speaks in hosts rather than a generic regex/contains/exact toggle: exact, subdomain (example.com and any *.example.com, end-anchored), and a regex that is labelled and documented as the full-string match it always was; the old contains mode is gone, because a substring match on an allowlist would have admitted example.com.attacker.com. Each settings tab now has its own URL (/admin/settings/network/ rather than ?tab=network), matching the stats and per-site pages. And every segment of the overview's composition card can be clicked in or out of the denominator, so the headline percentage reads against exactly the slice you want, with the selection kept in a cookie. Also fixed: the admin-host allowlist now honours its mode toggle and rejects a pattern it cannot compile instead of dropping it silently, and the composition breakdown popover separates its labels from its figures and stays put when pinned.

A challenge posture now costs what it names: a rule whose chain ends in a CAPTCHA is satisfied only by a CAPTCHA-grade pass. Until now any valid pass cookie exempted its holder, so a UA deliberately put behind a CAPTCHA walked through on a proof-of-work cookie - solvable by any headless runtime - and a silent re-bind extended that pass to new addresses without ever facing the CAPTCHA. Solves now record the grade they actually proved (a later CAPTCHA solve upgrades it), re-binds check it before extending a credential, and the built-in challenge-target presets arm the requirement on an ordinary install without writing a rule. The other half of the same production report is visibility: a pass earned by re-binding was counted as a CAPTCHA solve, because the plugin read the cookie's shape rather than the kind signed into it - so a crawler passing entirely by roaming looked like a quiet trickle of CAPTCHA passes while the challenge was being walked through. Re-bound passes are now named on both wires, and the stats page ranks how many distinct addresses one solved challenge has been re-bound onto - the one view in which distributed crawling is visible at all, since every individual request is a legitimate pass - beside the per-address reuse ranking, with cap and veto refusals alongside. Cookies minted while a site ran in monitoring mode are no longer mistakable for solves, and never satisfy a grade requirement. Also: the overview page reads its 24h counters from the hourly rollup instead of scanning the raw event log, which on a grown install took it from tens of seconds to instant with identical figures; paths on the stats page name their host and link there; and each pass KPI carries the requests existing cookies admitted beside the solves that minted them.

The dashboard's abandonment rate now counts only ordinary visitors: anything an operator's rule deliberately sends to a challenge is expected to leave without solving, and dividing those departures into the same rate made a bot-heavy site read 99% abandonment while the 34 real visitors underneath were invisible - the same window reads 4.8% now, and rule-targeted departures stay under the blocked figure where they belong. A schema migration can no longer wedge an install that already carries part of its work: a duplicate column used to abort the file before its index was created, permanently, with one log line per restart as the only symptom. Rendering the nginx conf now leaves unchanged files untouched, so their timestamps mean "when the config last changed" rather than "when a render ran", and doctor uses that to warn when a saved change was rendered but nginx was never reloaded - previously that gap read as healthy on every check. A leftover challenge_targets.all in config.yml gets a warning that names the real cost (being challenged is not being blocked; use an explicit UA row with action deny) instead of a generic unrecognized-key line. unmask version prints the commit it was built from. Release-side, publishing now verifies what is actually served from the client's URLs per format, and the stable index refuses to ship an artifact that differs from what the testing channel confirmed under the same name. Note: 0.1.22 was a testing-channel pre-release only; everything it carried ships in this release.

deny now denies. Every axis except the ban was consulted only when the visitor held no pass cookie, so the word meant "deny unless this client cleared a challenge at some point in the last week" - and against anything able to clear one, that is not a block. Measured on a production install: a crawler already removed from the rescue list solved the proof-of-work from 419 addresses and served itself 137,051 requests in a day through a UA row set to deny. Raising the difficulty cannot reach it, because the cookie lasts a week and the cost is one solve per address per week whatever the difficulty is. A resolved deny is now enforced beside the ban, ahead of anything that reads the cookie, on both the native and forward-auth paths; rescues still win, so nothing an operator exempted on purpose is affected. The overview also stopped counting some requests twice: a request carrying a pass cookie that also matched a bypass rule counted as both, 397,043 of 3,582,523 requests in a day on one install, and the human share is now a count rather than whatever was left over. New in this release: a pre-release channel, so a fix can be confirmed by whoever reported it before it ships - the confirmed file is copied into the stable repository rather than rebuilt, and the channel is configured everywhere but active nowhere unless asked for by name.

A visitor who left while the challenge page was holding lost the solve they had already made. The display hold added in the previous release ran at the moment the proof of work completed - ahead of the pass cookie, the beacon and the credential fetch - so closing the tab during a pause unmask itself imposed meant no cookie, no record of the solve, and a fresh challenge on the next request. It surfaced while measuring a difficulty change: splitting the window at the hour the hold reached the fleet, one node ran 2.20% abandonment without it and 17.9% with it, against an 11.87% baseline before either change. The hold was not merely mis-counting departures, it was causing them, and it was large enough to hide the improvement underneath. The completed-state paint stays where it was; only the wait moves, to after the cookie is written, so leaving during it now keeps the pass.

The challenge page's presentation is a setting rather than a hard-coded beat. Removing the artificial waits in the previous release left a ~150ms interstitial - a flash a visitor notices but cannot read, the worst perceptual band there is. The visible style, the default, now holds the page to a configurable minimum (800ms out of the box; 0 redirects the instant the solve lands) with the spinner turning, the wording unchanged and the progress bar resting at 100% rather than fading from wherever it had reached. The invisible style shows nothing but the themed background until a configurable reveal delay, so a fast device passes with nothing shown at all and only a visitor who is actually waiting sees the spinner and its explanation. A CAPTCHA escalation and every error screen appear immediately in both styles, the hold never delays the CAPTCHA leg, and it is never counted into the solve-time metrics. The traffic-composition card can now be read against the traffic unmask actually judged rather than against everything the server served: requests a bypass rule exempted are not a rounding error, and leaving them in the denominator halves every other share. Both readings are rendered at once, so switching is instant. Removed: challenge_targets.all, which said the same thing the Operating-mode bucket actions already say from a key no form has rendered in months - a default install behaves identically, and an operator who had set known_browser_action: pass alongside it will find that choice honoured instead of silently overridden. Fixed: that same toggle made hunt attribute every challenge to the operator's UA rules, so on an install challenging every visitor the rows the label exists for were lost in the crowd; the rate-limit funnel rollup wedged forever on the first hour containing an event with no verdict, retrying it every minute while the dashboard raw-scanned an ever-growing window; and lowering the proof-of-work difficulty broke the site silently until nginx reloaded - the module kept verifying against the old target, refusing three solves in four and looping the visitor - so render-nginx now says so before it happens.

Every rule field that takes a pattern now says how it is read - regex, contains, or exact - with a chip in the field that switches it and a placeholder that follows. Pasting the value you want to block is the obvious thing to do with a regular-expression field and it silently did not work: a User-Agent pasted verbatim compiles, passes every check, and matches that same string with its parentheses removed, which is nothing. This applies to every pattern list - UA allow and block, JA4 verdicts, honeypot, protected, bypass, geo and ASN exemptions, rate-limit paths - and an unmarked pattern is still a regex meaning exactly what it meant. A UA block-list rule can pin its own action, so a rule that needs a CAPTCHA no longer has to drag every other rule with it. Hunt now says why a challenge fired for the axis that fires most of them: a challenge raised by the operator's own UA rule was recorded as "none", because nginx fires it off a map variable and forwards no header saying so. The serve event also records which chain it offered and every row carries the explanation, so a CAPTCHA the page escalated into reads as the divergence it is. Acting on a hunt row no longer leaves the page - the UA and network buttons open a dialog like BAN beside them, and the UA dialog proposes the identifying token, counts what the pattern would match, and refuses one that does not match the UA it was built from. Requests a bypass rule let through are counted apart from people, so a package repository or an API served behind a bypass path stops landing in the human share. Fixed: every visitor was held for 1.5 seconds before the challenge let them through and the wait was entirely artificial - a display floor whose placeholder had drifted from the constant the server substitutes into it, plus 800ms padding the post-solve redirect (proof-of-work p50 1508ms to 389ms, abandonment 7.53% to 2.76% on the same node); browsers without TextEncoder could not solve the proof of work at all and looped on the challenge forever; the dashboard could report zero human visitors for a site that had them, and a remainder that cannot be computed now reads an em dash with the reason rather than a silent zero; and a visitor who merely changed IP was re-challenged instead of being silently re-bound.

The dashboard now says what a site's traffic is made of, counted in requests: bots passed on purpose, bots stopped, and the rest. The old figure counted distinct clients and reckoned only from clients that failed a challenge, so every crawler let through on purpose was missing from a number named after exactly that - and the unit ranked the same traffic in the opposite order from the load it causes, because a crawler sweeps a site from a handful of addresses while a distributed bot spreads a few requests over thousands. Visitors who loaded a challenge and walked away are subtracted rather than disclosed in a footnote. Every custom rule records when it was added and when it was last edited, including the value lists (defined sites, admin and metrics allowlists) - a rule outlives the reason it was written and the audit log is pruned on a retention window, so for anything older there was nothing left that could say when it arrived. The proof of work runs in a Web Worker: the fallback yields with setTimeout and browsers clamp a background tab's timers to one second, so a visitor who switched tabs waited about a minute instead of under one. Hunt can drill from a network into the requests behind it, its rank cards fold away to hand their width to the ones still open, and long values clip with the whole string one click away. The managed geo databases keep themselves current on a monthly switch, country and ASN independently, swapping in a download only after it verifies as readable. Running the CLI as root drops to the daemon's user - a command run under sudo left files the daemon could not read, and the failure was silent and delayed. Every path field states whether it takes a regular expression, and they all do now, uniformly. Fixed: a visitor sending no User-Agent was recorded and classified as unmask's own fetcher in forward-auth mode (60% of all events on the install where it surfaced); observe mode reported itself as "no attacks"; the Apache hook fired on internal redirects and sub-requests; a confirmed settings row still offered controls and changed when one was touched; and redirect exemptions restamped their own date on every save.

The default rate limit becomes three parallel axes - per-IP, per-JA4, per-IP+JA4 - each an always-visible row: a bot fleet rotating addresses never accumulates in a per-IP bucket but tends to share a TLS fingerprint, and the new JA4 row (off by default, crowd-sized thresholds) keeps counting while the addresses churn. Named zones can count against their own key, and rate-limit enforcement is now identical across deploy modes - path patterns match literally on both wires, no-path zones actually apply in native mode, and overlapping zones all count in parallel with deny outranking a challenge. The admin login and password reset throttle per address in the application, replacing a rate-limit preset that never fired. Settings value lists (admin allowlist, hostnames, metrics, sites, trusted LBs) render as confirmed rows with per-row off switches, notes and reordering, and a switched-off row is absent from every consumer while the self-lockout guard judges what is actually enabled. The hunt log tells apps, browsers and bot kinds apart with small marks, names in-app browsers over their engine token, distinguishes listed crawlers from self-declared bots with policy-aware wording, counts visible sessions in the pager, and pages correctly at every size - the boundary margin now covers real session spread, the 1000-row page no longer collapses to 100, and the fragment hint names all three reasons rows can be elsewhere, including another fleet node behind a load balancer.

Crawler names stop being passes: bots whose vendors publish egress IP ranges (Googlebot, Bingbot, GPTBot, ...) are now verified by address as standing policy, on by default - a spoofed vendor UA takes the challenge while the genuine crawler passes from the published ranges, and the per-row choices survive underneath for when the policy is switched off. Apple push-notification previews pass out of the box behind a TLS-fingerprint guard: subscribers' own devices have no vendor ranges to verify against, so the UA must be backed by Apple's cipher-suite hash instead of being one copyable header line. The hunt log reads better while it moves: sessions no longer arrive cut in half at page boundaries, following next no longer repeats rows the log's growth pushed down, user agents render as "Windows 10 - Chrome 126" with the raw string in the popover, a refused roaming rebind appears inside the session it interrupts, and a collapsed session shows its total duration. Looking up a support ref went from a full-table scan (53 seconds on a 3.4M-row database) to an indexed seek (9ms); events stored before the upgrade drop out of ref search and age out on the retention window. Per-site checkboxes now show the value actually in effect, a per-site logo appears in the theme previews, each network-allowlist row can carry a note, and the site-scoped challenge preview moved under /unmask/test/site/.

unmask now fits on a 1GB VPS, and the header-integrity axis stops charging genuine old browsers. Fixed: that axis read a Chromium-family User-Agent sending no Sec-CH-UA as a spoof tell, but client hints only shipped in Chromium 89 (2021-03) — so every older browser was flagged for something it could not send. A valid _bv cookie still passed them, so this was never a permanent lockout, but the tell never stops being true: the same visitor was asked again every time that cookie lapsed, and the behavioural CAPTCHA is hardest to clear on precisely the old touch handsets it caught. The axis now stays silent below Chromium 89 in both deploy modes. Changed: SQLite's cache_size and mmap_size are per-connection settings, so the previous flat 128MB + 256MB was really up to 8x each once dashboard queries ran in parallel — enough to OOM a small host. Both are now derived from the memory the process may actually use and split across the pool, with the limit looked for in the cgroup (the service's own path, not just the hierarchy root), /proc/meminfo, and finally sysinfo(2), which still answers under a hardened systemd unit that removes /proc. The pool is sized to the CPUs the process may use rather than a flat 8. Added: a Performance tab showing the detected memory limit and CPU count, what is in effect now, and what each preset would use on this host — Conservative / Standard / Generous / Custom, with the cache budget and pool size separately adjustable. Event write-batching settings moved there from Log management.

Per-site settings stop freezing: a site record now holds only what you actually set for it, and every other value keeps following the global one — previously, configuring a single knob for a site detached it from the global record for all the others, silently, so raising the global proof-of-work difficulty afterwards skipped every site you had ever touched. The challenge page's theme, colours and credit line move to the design settings where the logo already lived, so styling a site no longer creates challenge overrides nobody asked for; existing config files are read in their old shape and carried across on load. Added: a per-site delete (the override toggle only ever meant "inherit for now, keep my values", and nothing removed the record itself); PoW-cookie reuse in the cookie-reuse ranking, which is the only place a client riding one solved challenge is visible at all, since a request carrying a valid cookie fires no challenge and writes no event; and the source IP of every audited admin action, which nothing else on the box recorded once a load balancer was in front. Fixed: `unmask doctor` reported nginx config as out of date on any node that had pulled crawler IP ranges — it re-rendered without them and compared against the real thing, advising a re-render for a config that was already correct.

Escalation-axis observability, and a fix that makes one of those axes actually fire behind a load balancer. Fixed: 0.1.11's header-integrity axis required HTTP/2·3 as seen by nginx itself, so behind a TLS-terminating load balancer — which re-originates the backend hop as HTTP/1.1 — it never fired at all, silently, even when enabled; with a trusted LB configured it now keys off the LB-forwarded scheme (X-Forwarded-Proto, unspoofable via proxy_set_header) and within minutes of going live was catching spoofed-Chromium scrapers that had been sailing through. Added: every dashboard surface now shows WHY a visitor was escalated — the forced-CAPTCHA card attributes the header-integrity / ASN / country / stale-browser axes; the challenge funnel gains per-axis pseudo-rows whose pass rate reads as that axis's false-positive rate (the challenge page carries the reason through every phase beacon); the CAPTCHA pass report and the failure IP ranking break down by axis, with the reason on every row; and the bot-hunt raw log gets a reason column and filter. The funnel's per-row rate becomes a pass rate over everyone served (bv_total/serve; the CAPTCHA rate stays captcha-scoped). unmask doctor — and render-nginx, which package postinstalls run — now warns when nginx is still running on libraries replaced underneath it, where a plain reload would hand live traffic to workers built from a torn image (SIGSEGV, empty replies); it points at restart instead and stays silent when nothing is stale. Overview KPI tiles adopt the stats chart's bucket colours, and the header-integrity axis can escalate to pow_then_captcha.

Network-axis maturation. Verify a claimed crawler by reverse DNS (PTR → vendor domain → forward-confirm) so a genuine Googlebot/Bingbot/YandexBot/Applebot/Baiduspider is rescued even outside its published ranges while a forged one is challenged or auto-banned — asynchronous (no request latency), range-aware, per-crawler toggleable. Throttle a network or country instead of blocking it: ASN and country rules gain a per-minute rate that acts only on the overage, with a config default and per-row override, in both modes (native limit_req zone, forward-auth live count) and verified crawlers/bypass IPs exempt so SEO is never rate-limited. Exempt a path from just the country or ASN decision (RSS/Atom feeds from datacenter readers) while every other check keeps running. A new opt-in header-integrity axis challenges a Chromium UA that carries no Sec-CH-UA over HTTPS on h2/h3 — clamped to a challenge, silent on HTTP/HTTP1.1/Firefox/Safari/TLS-intercept proxies. The stale-browser lag is now settable per browser (Chrome and Firefox independently).

Fixes and cleanup. The 0.1.9 test-page site picker works again (its challenge could not be passed and the per-site logo did not show). Saving settings from the web UI no longer deletes config sections owned by other programs sharing config.yml. The forward-auth decision endpoint stops rebuilding its matchers on every request, and the SQLite page cache grows to 128MB for multi-GB event databases. FHS cleanup: the nginx module survives an immutable /usr via a /var/lib fallback, the Apache Lua hook payload moved to /usr/share (the /etc paths stay as symlinks), and the setup token moved to /var/lib. Breaking for hand-edited nginx wiring: both deploy modes now share ONE daemon upstream, `upstream unmask_daemon` (defined only in upstream.conf; http.inc no longer defines an upstream), and the daemon-down hook is `@unmask_daemon_down`. Packaged installs converge automatically on upgrade + re-render; if you hand-copied forward-auth/server.inc or hand-include the rendered files, update the names and include upstream.conf — `nginx -t` names anything left over.

Operational visibility and multi-site polish. The admin now tells you when the daemon cannot write its own database — a read-only DB (classically a root-owned unmask.sqlite left behind by running unmask migrate as root) keeps serving challenges while silently recording nothing; the retention tab runs an in-daemon write probe with a copy-pasteable fix, and unmask doctor gains the matching check. Per-site challenge logos now actually work (each scope gets its own file instead of overwriting a shared one), and the test pages gain a site picker so a multi-site install can exercise a specific site's challenge end-to-end. Uploaded logos and the setup-wizard token move from /etc/unmask to /var/lib/unmask where variable data belongs.

Settings-save fixes and clearer crawler-spoof visibility. Saving a settings tab no longer silently rewrites values you did not touch — a family of long-standing save bugs is fixed, including the one that pinned the UA black-list's challenge chain onto every challenge (that default action now fires only on an actual black-list match, in both deploy modes). The UA-filter checkbox and the Bypass-IP range presets become independent axes with a live 4-state badge showing each range-backed crawler's true rescue path, so one tab can no longer silently change the other's behavior. The stale-browser tier learns Firefox (ESR stays exempt) and its current-major baselines now auto-follow a daily unmask.sh feed, so the tier keeps tracking new browser releases without manual bookkeeping. The AI-crawler drill-down marks IP-range-verified crawlers with a shield and renames served to challenge — for those vendors the challenged count is spoofed traffic, not the real bot being blocked. Bot hunt gains a User-Agent search and one-click raw-log filters from the rankings. Admin pages now send no-store, so a redeployed dashboard shows its changes on a normal reload.

Security and performance. A spoofed crawler User-Agent no longer walks through the challenge: for vendors that publish official IP ranges (Google, Bing, DuckDuckGo, OpenAI, Perplexity, and now Apple and Amazon), the rescue rides the verified IP ranges instead of the forgeable UA string, so a fake Googlebot from outside Google's ranges is now challenged. A new opt-in stale-browser tier escalates a browser pinned to an outdated Chrome version to a CAPTCHA — the tell of a headless PoW-solving scraper that a real old browser can still clear. Adds four official IP-range presets (Applebot, Amazonbot, DuckAssistBot, Perplexity-User) and lets stats-exclude entries carry a title. The admin dashboard — stats, the landing overview, and settings — is dramatically faster on large multi-site installs: the 30-day charts and the funnel now read background-maintained hourly rollups instead of scanning the full per-site history, so a stats page that took six to eight seconds returns in about two.

Critical fix for a connection leak introduced by 0.1.5's compose mode. On nginx 1.17.6+, every composed challenge or rate-limit redirect left its client connection permanently orphaned; the orphans accumulated until nginx ran out of worker connections and stopped answering entirely — on a busy protected site, within hours. The fix pairs the module's internal redirect with the request-reference release nginx expects (the X-Accel-Redirect idiom). If you run 0.1.5 with nginx 1.17.6 or newer, upgrade now and restart nginx — a reload does not replace the loaded module, and only a restart releases connections already orphaned.

Two over-blocking bugs and a scale fix. A daemon restart used to silently rewrite every inherit-action ban as a hard block, so a honeypot ban configured as a recoverable challenge became an unappealable 403 on every upgrade or reboot; and a honeypot probe arriving on the plaintext port could earn an auto-ban covering the scanner's whole IP. Both are fixed. The stats and bot-hunt pages no longer slow down as stored events accumulate (a new `unmask db-analyze` builds the query-planner statistics SQLite never had), the admin dashboard no longer redirect-loops when a long session outlives its CSRF cookie, and the nginx module stops flooding error.log with uninitialized-variable warnings. The rate-limit/challenge composition is now selected by the host nginx version (1.17.6+) rather than deny-zone presence. Adds a dashboard card showing what the Community Bans feed actually stopped.

Admin-settings polish and a health-check safety net: unmask doctor now probes :80 as a load-balancer health checker and warns if a redirect would drop the node, the network tab's custom IP / host lists become structured add/delete rows instead of newline textareas (with a default-off private-networks preset for stats-exclude), the HTTPS-redirect exemptions adopt the preset/custom two-badge layout, you can delete the last row of any custom list, and the hunt log's clipped 'already BANned' pill is fixed and localized.

Theme-tab preview fixes and a preview-language selector: the preview no longer redirects to the site for operators who already hold a pass cookie, an 18-locale language dropdown lets you preview any language, the over-block banner renders its dash correctly, and unmask doctor warns when https_redirect is enabled but not yet rendered.

HTTP→HTTPS redirect option (off by default, LB-aware, ACME-exempt); bypass-path presets gain per-preset factory defaults (machine-access presets ON out of the box); access-log parser no longer drops the trip URL / UA on TLS-resumption lines; events-table tooltip dedup and sites-tab wording fixes.

Install-path fixes found by dogfooding: postinstall now always restarts onto the new binary (upgrade/reinstall admin-loop fix); protect.inc exempts the /unmask/ machinery when included at server scope; libcrypto detection falls back to nginx -V when ldd is silent (static OpenSSL builds); unmask doctor warns on server-scope protect.inc.
First public release of unmask.
